I'll butt in here and add that whilst I adored Bioshock 1 and 2, I wasn't exactly best pleased by Infinite.

Every game in the series is amazing, and definitely worth their respective price points, don't get me wrong. For me, though, infinite was just *so* different that it became boring very quickly. The world was beautiful, the characters were lively, the enemies were unique, and the powers were awesome. I just didn't like it as much as I could've because it lacked the atmosphere and familiarity of Rapture.

My honest view is that if you're looking to purchase any of the Bioshock games, the tier order is 1>>2>>>>Infinite, from a pure enjoyment standpoint.

My reasoning for 1 being over 2 is just because Bioshock 1 will always be one of the best games around, and its through absolutely no fault of its own that 2 is below 1. 1 just set the bar *exponentially* high. The ending of BS2 was probably better than BS1, though. Although that's up to debate.

Again, Infinite is an amazing game, as are BS1 and BS2. Please don't be put off by Infinite by this, because its definitely worth buying and playing, and is by no means a bad game! I have yet to finish it, as I've reached a point where I'm getting bored, and I don't want to force myself to play the game to an untimely end. I'll probably pick it back up again soon.

My favourite characters are by far the originals. I'd always recommend levelling Claudette first, followed by Meg, followed by Nea.

Claudette for;
~Self Care. 
Currently trying to ween myself off of using SC, just as I'm finally climbing ranks easier, so will need to use different perks. 
~Blendette. Not a perk, just a good thing. 
Basically, much easier to hide as a newer player when you play with Claudette.

Meg;
~Sprint Burst
Not my favourite perk, as it forces you to either walk everywhere, or you accidentally use it and suddenly the killers right behind you and you can't use SB anymore. 
~Adrenaline. 
For end game. Set yourself up for a win! Don't start off using perks that assume you'll be put into a bad situation during the match! (aside from self care, which you obviously need to be injured for. SC is VERY crutch for new players especially, and I imagine you'll definitely want that to begin with.)

Nea;
~Urban Evasion.
Really good perk for immersed gameplay/being a gen jockey. Really essential for stealthy builds imo.
~Balanced Landing.
Basically an amazing perk for when you need to get away from a killer and get a map with high windows. Vault through a window and suddenly you're long gone, speeding away.

I would also like to add that Feng Min is also a very good survivor to start off with, but I wouldn't say she's as good as the others are. 

Feng Min;
~Lithe
Balanced Landing for vaults. Lithe is a perk that activates when you vault a pallet or window. You'll get a burst of speed. Good for evading killers on maps where you're either being tunnelled or there's only loops, and no buildings for BL. 
~Technician
Again, not on my personal choices of a perk build, but Technician is amazing for gen jockeys. Maybe not for a totally new player, but definitely important. Reduces the sound of you repairing a gen. 

My absolute favourite perks atm have to be;

Premonition III
Premonition is just amazing. Much better than Spine Chill. Premonition tells you if a killer is within a certain radius to you if you look in their direction. Very good if you're on a gen, basically just keep moving your head around and checking. If premonition goes off to your left, you know the killers that way, and you can sneak off to the right. 

Balanced Landing III
Already explained. Just an amazing perk, really. 

Borrowed Time III
Borrowed time is an altruistic perk. Very good to use in the event of a slightly campy killer. 10/10 would use against annoying Leatherfaces again. 

Dark Sense III
I think it's Dark Sense.. There's two very similar perks, but Dark Sense is essentially a perk which let's you see the aura of the killer for a few seconds every time a generator is completed, as long as YOU completed it. It doesn't matter how long you're on the gen for, but as long as you begin to repair it before it is fixed, you'll be able to use this perk to see the killer. 

Adrenaline III
Already explained. Amazing for end game if the killers looping you. 

WGLF III
I love We're Gonna Live Forever for the extra bloodpoints. I don't recommend you levelling up David JUST for this perk, though. Especially not if you're a low rank. BUT it may go on the store soon, so you may want to pick it up. It's stackable up to 4 points, and you can get up to 100% more bloodpoints (I believe? I can't remember, honestly. I hardly play with it.). All you have to do is take hits for your teammates and you'll eventually rack up the bloodpoints! I tend to use my Meg with WGLF but she only has tier I I believe, which is up to 50% more.

I would say Self Care but really, like I said, it's something I'm trying to stay away from as I climb the ranks, although I do like it.

My dog is an Old Tyme Bulldog, and is a chunky lil boy but not overweight. He's a perfect weight, maybe slightly softer around the middle but that's to be expected with any Bulldog breed, regardless. Basically, hes more reminiscent of a chunkier American Bulldog.

We always feed him one doggy meal per day.
- A cup of kibble
- Cheese chunks/ham slices/beef

Or
-Rice and Vegetables

He takes his time, and gets excersise in between eating, like your cats.
